My younger son was engaged on the line and he was there for a while. After that he was released and then he also went to Germany but none of us had work obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN DAMJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you for giving evidence to the Tribunal. We are finished. You may leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the next witness comes in, could we please move to private session so that I could make one request?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we move to private session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is of the view that on the basis of the explanation from the Defence counsel, the Trial Chamber is -- has accepted to grant a pseudonym and facial distortion to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may suggest, the witness be given the pseudonym TW 8/3 [as interpreted]. [In English] I said D. D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In which case, identifying marks will be redacted from his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. This is what I wanted to suggest as well. I've already informed the Prosecutors, Your Honour. I have a small correction to his written statement which we discovered when we were doing the proofing. In paragraph 9, the last sentence states, "1992." And the witness, and I explained that to the Prosecutor, was on work obligation throughout 1993. So the correction is made to the year. If necessary, I will make an annex in -- a written annex to the statement and provide that to the Chamber, correcting that year in that paragraph of the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't see why it can't be corrected on the record so that we have 1993 instead of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go back into open session now that the witness has come in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have copies of the redacted statement for the Chamber and the Registry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are already in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the beginning of your testimony, I will tell you that the Trial Chamber has granted you protective measures. You will be given a pseudonym. Your details will be known only to the Chamber and the participants in this trial. You have been granted facial distortion so that your identity cannot be established outside this courtroom. I would like to ask you not to mention your name and the name of your family members. If it is necessary to mention these names we will go into private session, but all the details concerning your identity are known to the Trial Chamber from your written statement so we need not discuss this here. Do you understand all this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber also has before it your written statement describing in detail your stay in Samac before and during your detainment. We have entered the correction saying that you had work obligation from 1963 [as interpreted]. And now I will put questions to you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter corrects herself, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will now talk to two parts of your statement that we have already discussed. Your stay in Batkovic and your exchange. The first thing I will ask you, sir: Did all of you who were in Samac together, where you were, and you can tell the Chamber, because it's not in the record where you were detained in Samac, were you all taken to Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: In Samac, I was detained in the SUP for five months, and about ten days. On the 27th of November, we were all taken to Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you tell the Chamber how many of you prisoners were taken from Samac to Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: About 150 or 180, around that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, all of you from Samac or rather the detainees from Samac who were taken to Batkovic, were you all placed in the same hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: There were two hangars, one next to the other. In the left-hand one, there were perhaps about 90 per cent of us, and the rest were in the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you about several of your fellow citizens and please tell me if they were in the same hangar as you in Batkovic. Do you know a man named Ibrahim Salkic, known as Ibela, was he with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes, I know him and he was in the hangar together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Kemal Mehinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Reuf Hadziabdic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Izet Hamusevic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Salko Porobic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am especially interested in a fellow citizen of yours. Did you know a man named Sabah Seric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him. He is related to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excellent. That's what we need in order to identify him fully. Do you know his father's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He bears the same first name as me, [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This Sabah Seric, did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes, they called him Sanak [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where he worked before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes. He worked in the iron work store.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the part of the record where the witness mentioned his name be redacted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Don't mention your name by any means. Tell us: In Samac, at the time, you said that the man was related to you. Was there another Saban Seric in Samac, was there another Seric with a same or similar first name of Sabah?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: No. There was only one Sabah Seric. As for Safet, Safet was his brother, who was killed in a traffic accident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this before the war that his brother was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we have clarified some points now. Sir, do you remember in the period while you were in the Batkovic camp, how many exchanges were organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: I remember the 6th of January, 1993, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I know what you want to say, but I don't want you to say this because of your identity. Do you remember that there was an exchange on that date? That's all I want to know. We know why.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: I remember my exchange on the 29th of January, 1993. I know that towards the end of December, there was an exchange in 1992. But I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On those occasions, the three occasions you mentioned, when exchanges were organised, do you remember whether on those occasions you saw Miroslav Tadic? But first, I will ask you, did you know Miroslav Tadic before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes, I did, although we didn't move in the same circles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in your statement. Now just answer this: In Batkovic, when these exchanges were taking place, did you see Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you always see him on the day when an exchange was organised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: On the 6th of January, a soldier was reading out the list. He was standing next to the soldier. As soon as the list was read out, the detainees were told to pack because they were going to be exchanged. Mr. Tadic left the compound, and on that day, I didn't see him again. When I was exchanged on the 29th, he was also there. A soldier read out names. I don't remember the soldier's name. And he was standing to one side. They left the compound right away and we were told to pack. We left the compound. We were lined up and underwent a cursory search. Then we were told we could board the bus. The bus was from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll come to your exchange. We won't talk about it just yet. I'd like to ask you a few more questions about the procedure during the exchange. Or rather the reading out of names. In the period while you were in Batkovic, in December and January, as far as I can see, during those two months, tell us, did you hear or see that someone's name was called out who was not exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: No. I don't know who would give his place to someone else. Who would remain behind and give his place to someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What would happen if someone wasn't present at the moment his name was called out? What happened in such cases, if they happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Well, it did happen sometimes. They would go and fetch them in a van, to -- they would go to where they were working and bring them back to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the prison, was there talk of someone going whose name had not been called out? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: Well, we constantly discussed it, or rather we constantly discussed exchanges, when there would be an exchange, when it would be someone's turn. We talked about it all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see, sir, when names were read out, or after they were read out, people approaching Tadic, talking to him? Were they able to approach him or address him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW 8/3
utterances.text: No. Because we were all listening to the roll call, and as soon as it was over, he would leave. He would leave the compound. And the people would go and get their things and get ready to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like to start on a different topic so this might be a convenient moment now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will continue with the witness tomorrow. But before we rise, I wanted to confirm with you, Mr. Lukic that you received the consent for the demographer, the expert witness to be given the documents by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Today in my locker, I received the submission that we asked for. I haven't had a chance to talk to the Prosecutor yet, but I hope I will be able to get our expert here next week because now all the technical prerequisites have been met for us to finish our expert report. I have to contact her and see whether she is able to arrive next week but I'm sure there will be no problem. First I will discuss the technical details with the Prosecution, how it will be made possible for her and her associate to look into the documentation but I believe we will have no problems in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I just want confirmation from the Prosecution that they also received the authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Haven't seen it. Can't confirm one way or the other. We will certainly know by tomorrow morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It was filed on the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All I can say is today is the 31st. I haven't seen it. I'm not saying we haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, what I'm saying is I want the Prosecution to deal with the matter as quickly as possible so that we don't drag on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I said I can tell you tomorrow morning. I just haven't seen it. Mr. Di Fazio and I haven't seen it. It was filed on Friday. We have been in court this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But you have members of your staff who are working behind the scenes on these matters. So the Prosecution is expected to make available the documents that were made available to them for the purposes of this expert witness for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour there is one matter could I briefly raise about a witness tomorrow morning? One of the Defence witnesses, Mr. Tubakovic, whose statement is D184/3? It seems upon my perusal of the transcript of the 21st of March, at page 17235, and Your Honour's orders in relation to excluding part of it, Your Honour's order in relation to paragraph 22 was the first two sentences which discuss the acts and conduct of the accused are also struck off. That may be an error because the first two sentences say life in Samac during the war was difficult. The Croatian Army and HVO started shelling Samac. It's the sentences after that which actually discuss the acts and conduct of the accused. I raise that now lest the wrong sentences be redacted and to give Your Honours a chance to revisit it perhaps overnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the number that was given to the statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we'll check it and see whether it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Defence for Mr. Simo Zaric is expected to bring some witnesses so that we continue this week as we are moving fairly fast with the witnesses for Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour maybe I can inform the Trial Chamber in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You have probably noticed that I didn't come after the previous break here and I was really trying to do my best and I am doing my best to bring the witnesses here. But I believe I have to inform the Trial Chamber and I already raised this issue with the Prosecution, and with the registry as well, none of our witnesses will be ready to come here before Thursday due to many circumstances. Your Honours are aware that there were supposed to be here, and then there was an information from the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I will cut you short. The Trial Chamber was informed by the legal officer as to the status of affairs in the Victims and Witnesses Unit. There are some witnesses or at least there is one witness who has a permanent visa and that witness can be flown over quickly and others whom arrangements can be made quite fast. So the Trial Chamber is well informed by the Victims and Witnesses Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you. This helps me in a way but I only thing I would like to inform that this one witness that already has a visa is actually Mr. Zaric's wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I expect the Defence counsel to work hard and bring more than that one witness so that we can continue working through the witnesses and see if we can complete them as quickly as possible. We'll rise now and continue our proceedings tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
